any.topic: Data kept in the country or the EU
any.answer: All customer data, copies, and management and monitoring data stay in [the EU / the country], in [the customer's data centres / the named region]. Nothing leaves it for support or telemetry unless the customer allows it.
evidence: Where every component and its data run
The data processing terms for support and telemetry
any.check: Check where the management plane, support uploads and telemetry go, not only the workloads.

any.answer: [The vendor / the partner] holds [the certifications, with their scope and expiry]; the certificates are attached.
evidence: The certificates, with scope and expiry
any.check: Check that each certificate's scope covers what is offered, and that it is still valid on the due date.

any.answer: Training for [number] administrators is included: [courses, hands-on sessions, knowledge transfer during delivery], in [language], with [the materials].
evidence: The training plan: topics, hours, format
any.check: Agree who delivers it: the vendor, the partner, or both.

any.answer: Support is available [24x7 / in business hours] in [language], with response times of [times by severity]; [the vendor / the partner] is the first point of contact.
evidence: The support terms, with response times by severity
any.check: Match the response times to the tender's service levels and penalties.

any.answer: Data is encrypted at rest [with software or self-encrypting drives], with keys held in [a built-in key manager / the customer's key manager]; data between sites is encrypted [how].
evidence: The encryption design and the key manager used
The cryptographic validation, if the tender asks for one
any.check: Check whether the tender requires an external key manager or a validated cryptographic module.

hci.topic: Keeps running through a node failure
hci.answer: The platform keeps running when a node fails: data is kept in [two / three] copies across nodes, and the machines of a failed node restart on the others automatically. The design tolerates [the failures].
evidence: The proposed design, with the failures it tolerates
The failure test from the proof of value
hci.check: Confirm the number of nodes and the copy setting in the sizing.

hci.answer: The whole stack (firmware, hypervisor and storage software) is upgraded one node at a time, with the machines moved off each node first, so they keep running; upgrades start from the management console.
evidence: The upgrade procedure
An upgrade run during the proof of value, with its log
hci.check: Check which components the platform's upgrade covers and which the hardware maker's tools do.

hci.answer: Running machines move between nodes without stopping, for maintenance or balancing; the hypervisor is included in the offer.
evidence: The hypervisor features included in the offer
hci.check: Check that the licence edition offered includes it.

hci.answer: Capacity grows by adding nodes to a running cluster, without stopping it; nodes of [different generations or sizes] can be mixed within [the limits].
evidence: The expansion procedure and its limits
hci.check: State the limits of mixing node models and generations honestly.

dr-backup.answer: Each tier gets its own recovery point and time: [tier 1: RPO, RTO; tier 2: ...]. Replication to [the second site / the cloud] runs [continuously / every N minutes], within [the bandwidth measured].
evidence: The recovery design per tier, with the bandwidth it needs
A test failover's measured times
dr-backup.check: Check the recovery point against the measured change rate and bandwidth before promising it.

dr-backup.answer: At least one copy is immutable for [days]: nobody, administrators included, can delete or change it before then. Restores from it are tested [how often].
evidence: How the immutable copy is enforced, and by what
A delete refused during the proof of value
dr-backup.check: Check whether an administrator could shorten the retention or reset the system.

dr-backup.answer: Failover is tested on an isolated network while production runs: the recovery plan starts the copies, checks them, and cleans up afterwards. Test reports are kept.
evidence: A test failover report
dr-backup.check: Agree how often it is tested and who reads the report.

dr-backup.answer: Recovery plans set which machines start, in what order, with which addresses and networks at the recovery site; they run with one action, for a test or a real failover.
evidence: A recovery plan for one application
dr-backup.check: Check that network changes (addresses, DNS, firewall rules) are covered, not only the machines.

dr-backup.answer: Copies are kept for [retention per tier], [on local storage / object storage / off site], with [the number of] versions.
evidence: The retention design, with the capacity it needs
dr-backup.check: Size the capacity for the whole retention, not for one copy.

object-storage.answer: Object storage with an S3-compatible interface is offered for [usable capacity], with [versioning, lifecycle rules, replication between sites] as needed.
evidence: The S3 operations supported
A test with the customer's backup software
object-storage.check: Check that the customer's applications and backup software are validated with it.

object-storage.answer: Objects can be locked for a set time, so nobody can delete or overwrite them before it ends; in [compliance mode] not even administrators can shorten it.
evidence: The lock modes, and who can change what
object-storage.check: Check which mode the backup software uses.

object-storage.answer: [Usable capacity] after protection, from [the design]; capacity grows by adding [nodes / disks] without stopping the service.
evidence: The capacity calculation, raw to usable
object-storage.check: State usable capacity, not raw, and the protection setting behind it.

file-storage.answer: File shares over SMB [versions] and NFS [versions] are provided, with permissions from [the directory], for [the departments and sites].
evidence: The protocols and versions supported
file-storage.check: Check shares used over both protocols at once, if any.

file-storage.answer: Snapshots are taken [every N hours] and kept for [days]; users restore their own files from previous versions, without a ticket.
evidence: The snapshot schedule and retention
file-storage.check: Size the capacity for the snapshot retention.

file-storage.answer: Every access and change to files can be recorded and searched (who, what, when), and unusual activity such as mass encryption raises an alert [and blocks the user].
evidence: An audit search and an anomaly alert from the proof of value
file-storage.check: Check how long audit records are kept, and where.

cloud-operations.answer: Teams order approved services from a catalog, within quotas and with approvals where required; every request is logged. The first items are [the catalog items].
evidence: The catalog design, with quotas and approvals
cloud-operations.check: Agree who owns each catalog item.

cloud-operations.answer: Each team's or project's cost is shown monthly, from a unit cost agreed with finance; it can be charged back once agreed.
evidence: The cost model, and one month's report
cloud-operations.check: Agree the cost elements with finance first.

cloud-operations.answer: Health, performance and capacity are monitored from one console, with a forecast of when each cluster runs out and alerts on unusual behaviour.
evidence: A capacity forecast report
cloud-operations.check: Check how long monitoring data is kept, and where.

edge-sites.answer: Every site is managed from one central console (health, versions, upgrades, alerts). Sites run [one / two / three]-node clusters sized per kind of site, and keep working if their link drops.
evidence: The design per kind of site
edge-sites.check: Check where the witness runs for two-node sites.

edge-sites.answer: Sites are upgraded remotely in waves, starting with a pilot site of each kind; no visit is needed.
evidence: The upgrade plan in waves
edge-sites.check: Check each link's bandwidth for the upgrade downloads.

edge-sites.answer: Servers ship ready to join the central console on their own: someone without IT skills plugs them in.
evidence: The procedure for a new site
edge-sites.check: Agree who ships the servers and who plugs them in.

euc.answer: Virtual desktops for [number] users at peak are sized at [resources per user], with [the desktop software offered], on the same platform; logon time is measured in the proof of value.
evidence: The desktop sizing
The logon times measured
euc.check: Check that the desktop software licence is in the offer, and who supplies it.

platform-migration.answer: Existing machines move in waves after a test wave; each wave has a window, a checklist and a rollback to the source platform. [The tool, and who runs it.]
evidence: The migration plan in waves
The test wave's report
platform-migration.check: Check the inventory first: machines switched off or out of support should not move as they are.

kubernetes-platform.answer: Kubernetes clusters are created, upgraded and scaled from one console, with persistent storage and backup of workloads with their data. [The versions supported.]
evidence: The Kubernetes versions supported, and the upgrade policy
kubernetes-platform.check: Check the supported versions against the customer's.

private-ai.answer: Models run on [GPUs] in the customer's data centre: data and prompts stay there. Endpoints have access control and quotas. [The models validated.]
evidence: The GPU sizing for the models and users
private-ai.check: Check each model's licence for the intended use.

dbaas.answer: Databases are created, patched, copied and restored to a point in time from one console; copies for testing can be masked.
evidence: A point-in-time restore and a copy, timed
dbaas.check: Check the database engines and versions supported.

microsegmentation.answer: Traffic between machines is seen first, then restricted by policies that follow the machines when they move or fail over; environments can be isolated and a machine quarantined.
evidence: Traffic seen before the policies, from the proof of value
microsegmentation.check: Agree who owns the policies after delivery.

service-provider-cloud.answer: Tenants are kept apart on shared infrastructure, each with its own networks (overlapping addresses allowed), identity and quotas, and manage their resources within the provider's limits.
evidence: The isolation design and its test
service-provider-cloud.check: Check that the metering export fits the billing system.

cnapp.answer: Every account, subscription and project in [the clouds in scope] is connected at the organisation level, so new ones are covered the day they are created; [N] are in scope today.
evidence: The accounts the tool sees, compared with the bill
How a new account is connected without a ticket
cnapp.check: Check that accounts created outside the organisation, and regions turned off, are counted too.

cnapp.answer: Each finding reaches the team that owns the resource in [the ticketing tool], with a due date by severity: [critical: N days; high: N days]. Accepted risks need an owner and an end date.
evidence: A finding followed from detection to its ticket
The severity and due-date rules
cnapp.check: Check how ownership is known: tags, account owners, or a mapping someone has to keep.

siem.answer: Logs are searchable for [N months] and kept for [N years] in cheaper storage that can still be searched on request, within [the regulation or policy named in the tender].
evidence: The retention per log source and tier
A search on an archived log, timed
siem.check: Check the cost of the retention asked for at the expected daily volume, not only that it is possible.

siem.answer: The sources in scope [list] are collected with [built-in connectors / agents / syslog]; a source that stops sending raises an alert within [time].
evidence: The list of sources with how each is collected
An alert when a source goes quiet, shown
siem.check: Check the sources the tender lists one by one, including the custom applications.

siem.answer: The response to [the common alerts named] is automated with playbooks: [contain, enrich, notify]. Actions that change production need [an approval step].
evidence: A playbook run end to end
Which actions need approval
siem.check: Check which systems the playbooks can act on, and with what rights.

identity.answer: Strong multi-factor is required for [all users / privileged users], [phishing-resistant methods] for administrators, with no standing exceptions; service accounts use [managed secrets / certificates].
evidence: The sign-in policy as configured
A week of privileged sign-ins, all with strong authentication
identity.check: Check legacy protocols and service accounts: they are where multi-factor is usually bypassed.

identity.answer: Access is granted and removed from [the HR system] as the source: a leaver loses every access in scope within [time], applications outside the directory included through [connectors / tickets].
evidence: A leaver followed to the last access removed
The applications connected, and those that are not
identity.check: Check the applications with their own accounts outside the directory.

endpoint.answer: The agent supports [the systems and versions in scope]; [N] devices are covered, and the unsupported systems in scope are [isolated / monitored by other means].
evidence: The support matrix for the versions in scope
Agents reporting, compared with the inventory
endpoint.check: Check the oldest systems in the tender, and servers that cannot take an agent.

endpoint.answer: A compromised device can be isolated in one action, [automatically for the clearest cases], at any hour, while it stays reachable for investigation.
evidence: An isolation timed during the proof
The rules for automatic isolation
endpoint.check: Check who answers out of hours: the team or a service, and with what rights.

saas.answer: The tenants in scope [list] are connected read-only; settings, admin roles, third-party apps and public sharing are checked against [the baseline named].
evidence: The tenants connected and the checks run on each
A risky setting found and fixed
saas.check: Check which applications the tender names, and whether each is supported with its own checks.

ai.answer: The AI services, models and agents in use are listed with an owner, from [network, spend and sign-in records]; agents are listed with the tools they can call and what each can change.
evidence: The inventory and how it is kept current
One agent's tools and their rights
ai.check: Check how a team starting a new AI service is found without telling anyone.

ai.answer: Sensitive data is checked before it reaches a prompt or a retrieval index, [blocked / masked], and what was sent is logged for [N months].
evidence: A test prompt with invented sensitive data, caught
Where prompts and answers are logged
ai.check: Check the services reached outside the controlled path, such as personal accounts.
